assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin biology led from the discovery of GLP-1 physiology to drugs that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal outcome benefits. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are exceptional and rest on a coherent chain from physiology to therapy.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology, GLP-2, DPP-4 axis), Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action) and Knudsen (design of long-acting liraglutide/semaglutide) cover mechanism through drug. Mojsov's early peptide characterization is a real claim and the history, including contributions from Habener's group, who is not on this list, is contested; I leave her off with that caveat.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by large independent randomized trials and wide clinical use; timing is highly appropriate and the case has become more urgent each year.
uncertainties: Fair allocation of credit for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) form is disputed and cannot be resolved from the supplied names.
Long-term safety and durability of effects in obesity are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed by chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and have opened a new modality of cellular therapy. The concept is original and the clinical impact is clear.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T with costimulatory domains in CLL and ALL) and Sadelain (second-generation costimulatory CAR design) are the strongest pair among those credited. Rosenberg's adoptive-transfer and early CAR work is important but arguably adjacent. Early CAR concepts from outside this list, notably Eshhar's, complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation in hematologic cancers; solid tumours remain unresolved, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Priority among first-generation CAR concepts and clinical translation is not fully settled.
Toxicity, relapse and limited solid-tumour efficacy qualify the long-term picture.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and established the paradigm of targeted kinase-inhibitor therapy based on a defined oncogenic driver. Clarity and impact are outstanding.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (drug programme and the kinase-inhibitor concept), Druker (clinical proof of principle and trials) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. Slamon and others are outside this entry; the Abl/BCR-ABL oncogene discovery itself was earlier and is separate.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent follow-up and several generations of inhibitors; fully mature, with a risk that recognition seems overdue relative to peers.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as drug development rather than a discovery in physiology is a judgement call.
Role of earlier BCR-ABL work and industry contributions may complicate a fair three-person split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic in which the endoplasmic reticulum communicates its folding state to the nucleus. It is an original and conceptually clear discovery with wide relevance to disease, including neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Mori (yeast and mammalian UPR transcriptional response) and Walter (Ire1 and the mechanism of signalling, later ISRIB) form a natural pair. Ron's later work on PERK/eIF2 is not credited here, and Hartl-Horwich style chaperone work is a separate candidate.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed across systems for many years; therapeutic extension remains partial, but the basic discovery is mature and Lasker-recognized.
uncertainties: Disease-level translation is less established than the basic mechanism.
Omission of branches of the pathway from the credited names may be questioned.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics allows causal control of defined cell populations with light and has reshaped neuroscience, with first clinical applications in vision restoration. The methodological impact is very large and the discovery chain from channelrhodopsin to neuronal use is clear.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth (with Boyden) made the tool work in neurons and the in vivo use. Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck all have real claims, so any three-person configuration leaves out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Broadly validated and ubiquitous in research; clinical use is early but the technology itself is mature.
uncertainties: Constraining credit to three people is difficult and contentious.
Medicine relevance is mainly as a research tool so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BCL-2 family established that cell survival is actively controlled, linking apoptosis to cancer and enabling the BH3-mimetic venetoclax. The discovery is clear and consequential for both cell biology and therapy.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterized the BCL2 translocation and the family, and Vaux showed its anti-apoptotic function and cooperation with MYC. Strasser contributed to the BH3-only family; the credit is closer to a two- or three-person case than a four-person one. Other BCL-2 pioneers outside this list, such as Korsmeyer and Tsujimoto, complicate attribution.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation across decades and a validated drug; apoptosis itself already recognized in 2002, which may weigh against.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 apoptosis prize may reduce perceived novelty.
Several early BCL-2 contributors are not on the list, so attribution is not clean.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers, with population data showing steep drops in precancer and cancer. A clear, original discovery with major public-health impact.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP formation and immunogenicity) and Frazer (the vaccine development with Zhou, who has died) are the principal credited names. The role of other groups (Kirnbauer, Rose and others) is a recognized question.
assessment.maturity: Long-term population-level evidence of efficacy in several countries; recognition is timely and still gaining strength.
uncertainties: Contemporaneous VLP contributions by other groups may complicate allocation.
Final cancer endpoints still emerging in cohorts vaccinated later.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identified the neuropeptide system whose loss causes narcolepsy type 1, and has yielded a mechanistic understanding of sleep-wake stability and orexin receptor antagonists as drugs. The clarity of the disease link is a strength; I assess this as I would any field, with no preference arising from my own neurology background.
assessment.attribution: Yanagisawa and Sakurai identified orexins and their receptors; Mignot's canine genetics (Hcrtr2) and human work established the disease link, while de Lecea and Kilduff's hypocretin work was near-simultaneous. The configuration is credible but leaves out some legitimate co-discoverers.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation of orexin neuron loss and approved receptor antagonists support maturity; orexin agonists in late clinical development may add to it.
uncertainties: Dual discovery by two groups with credit allocation to de Lecea and Kilduff is unresolved.
The disease's rarity limits the sense of broad clinical impact relative to other candidates.
